name: Confirm the Placeholder numbers the results rest on
owner: Logistics, Site operations, Engineering and Sourcing
protects: It protects against every risk. Six internal figures decide whether the first failure in each future is real: days of helium on hand at the United States plant, the plant's backup power, the helium a sealed magnet draws in testing (in liters), where the cold-head maker and the wire mill sit relative to the Nankai Trough earthquake zone off Japan, the weeks of logic parts held at the China plant, and the price at which the OEM loses its helium allocation.
why_now: Every other action is sized from these numbers, and all of them are synthetic today. All 11 panel members ranked this action first or second.
too_late_after: It is too late once the 2027 sourcing cycle opens on synthetic numbers.
act_if: Act now, and ask again any function that has not returned its number by the end of 2026.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again if a confirmed number moves a first failure by a quarter, or shows that a failure costs money but stays inside the 30-day limit.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a year of decisions sized on guesses and a capital plan built on synthetic numbers.

name: Test a 30-day manual fallback at both plants and both sole suppliers against a 35-day systems outage
owner: Site operations with Sourcing, with the wire mill and the cold-head maker taking part
protects: It protects the United States plant, the China plant, the wire mill, the cold-head maker, the gas carriers and the port terminal. A 35-day systems outage is the one failure that every future shares, and it falls wherever each future's first failure already sits.
why_now: No outside event will warn of the shared failure, so the test sets the only deadline. All 11 panel members say it works in every future. The people who ran the line on paper are the ones nearest retirement.
too_late_after: It is too late after the first outage, or once the people who can write the manual procedure have retired.
act_if: Act if any site cannot say today how it would ship without its systems, or if a sole supplier or a peer in the sector reports a systems outage of a week or more.
pause_if: Pause once a site has passed a timed test twice.
look_again_if: Look again after any systems migration, if a test fails, or if the drill assumed the grid and the roads were working.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves another year in which a 35-day stop pushes the line past the 30-day limit in every future. The stop is largely uninsured, because cyber insurance excludes acts by states.

name: Qualify a second cold-head maker
protects: It protects the cold head, and through it both plants and the installed scanners. It removes the first failure in Future 2 and Future 4, and it reduces the cost of a cold-head outage in Future 1 and Future 3, where helium is the fallback. Four panel members (Foreign trade and payments, Geopolitical, Technology shift and Contrarian) say it works in all four futures, because the same cold head also cools conventional magnets. The other seven limit it to the futures where sealed magnets take over.
why_now: Requalification takes 18 months, and in Future 4 the cold heads fail by 2029, so a start after mid-2027 comes too late. The Contrarian member's condition stands: one maker has already left the market, so the action becomes real only once Sourcing names a second maker with a letter of intent.
too_late_after: It is too late after the end of 2027.
act_if: Act if Sourcing names a second maker with a letter of intent, if sealed magnets pass a quarter of new clearances, or if a producer country's export-control register names cryocoolers or cold heads.
pause_if: Pause if no second maker exists, and switch to the supply agreement (A2) and the 30-day hold (A7) instead. Also pause if sealed magnets stay below a quarter of clearances in 2028 and conventional builds still dominate.
look_again_if: Look again if the parent company announces a review or exit of its cryogenics unit, if a second maker sits inside the same Nankai Trough earthquake zone, or if the cold head's own suppliers are shared (A24).
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means the second source arrives after the Future 4 failure and after a tender cycle. In Future 4 both plants stay stopped into 2030.

name: Keep an offline, restore-tested copy of the design and qualification record
principle: Resilient products and processes (intellectual property ownership and continuity)
protects: It protects the design and qualification record, and through it every 18-month requalification of a site or supplier. Every future assumes the record is intact, and nothing on the starting list of actions kept it that way.
why_now: The Security and Contrarian members proposed it independently. Losing the record would make every replacement time unknown, and the manual fallback test (A9) works only if the record survives.
too_late_after: It is too late after the first systems outage.
act_if: Act if nobody has ever timed a restore of the record.
pause_if: Pause if a timed restore within 30 days already exists.
look_again_if: Look again after any cyber attack on the OEM or a sole supplier.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves the assumption that every future rests on unchecked for another year.

name: Keep more days of helium on hand at the United States plant than a container's hold time plus the 10-day grid rebuild
protects: It protects the United States plant and its helium on hand. It removes the first failure in Future 1 and the second failure in Future 3. In Future 2 and Future 4 it only adds carrying cost.
why_now: In Future 1 the helium runs out in the winter of 2028 to 2029, and it could happen in any hurricane season from 2027. Helium stock builds slowly at allocated volumes and cannot be bought once the shortage starts. On 11 Oct 2026 the indicators lean toward the two futures where this action pays off.
too_late_after: It is too late after the 2028 hurricane season.
act_if: Act if Logistics reports fewer days of helium on hand than a container's hold time plus 10 days, if Gulf strait traffic stays below a quarter of normal into 2027, or if an allocation letter cuts the plant's monthly volume.
pause_if: Pause if the Gulf strait reopens to insured shipping and the allocation letters stop.
look_again_if: Look again if a United States helium allocation rule is proposed, if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder, or if the extra test capacity in A8 raises the plant's helium use.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks one 30 to 45 day stop at the United States plant and a quarter of Western installs arriving late (panel estimate).

name: Put the liquefier at the United States plant on backup power separate from the plant's power feed
protects: It protects the United States plant and its helium on hand. It covers the most ordinary failure on the map of sites and suppliers, a winter power curtailment, and it does no harm in the other futures.
why_now: The grid reliability body rates the Carolinas grid elevated from 2027 and the Midcontinent grid high from the winter of 2028. A generator takes a year to procure, and data centers are buying the same units. The Contrarian member warns that the panel will underrate this action because it is small.
start_by: In the 2027 capital plan, with procurement by mid-2027
too_late_after: It is too late after the winter of 2028.
act_if: Act if Site operations confirms that the liquefier shares the plant's power feed, or if the grid operator issues a winter curtailment notice for the region.
pause_if: Pause if the power feed is reclassified as a critical load, or if the plant holds more than 60 days of helium on hand.
look_again_if: Look again if sealed magnets pass half of output, if the switchgear can be reached from the plant network, or if the backup fuel supply crosses the feed's flood zone.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks a winter in which the liquefier sits idle through the first curtailment.

name: Hold more logic and cold-head stock at the China plant than the export license queue takes to clear
protects: It protects the China plant and its supply of logic parts and cold heads. It is the only action that has to move before Question 1 is answered, and it has the nearest deadline on the list.
why_now: The panel's first reading of the truce notice date is 10 Nov 2026. Stock bought after an export-control listing may itself need an export license. Three panel members add Future 4, where the stock absorbs a listing of the logic parts.
too_late_after: It is too late once an entity listing names the plant or its logic supplier.
act_if: Act if the truce is not renewed at its notice date, or if a listing names any supplier to the China plant.
pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed for a year or more with no listing.
look_again_if: Look again once Sourcing states the stock in weeks, if the license queue shortens, or if the warehouse sits in the flood plain.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means that in Future 3 the plant fails with empty shelves, and the stop lasts the whole license queue.

name: Sign a multi-year supply agreement with the cold-head maker's parent company, with a change-of-control clause and step-in rights to tooling and drawings
protects: It protects the supply of cold heads if the parent company sells or leaves the business. Nine panel members limit it to Future 4, because a contract changes neither an export license nor a flood. The Financial member says it works in all four futures if it carries a change-of-control clause.
why_now: The 2027 sourcing cycle is the last normal negotiation before the parent's next capacity review. A single sale document could end the line.
too_late_after: It is too late once the parent announces a sale, a review or an exit.
act_if: Act if the parent's filings show its cryogenics unit shrinking, under review or below the group's margin.
pause_if: Pause if A1 qualifies a second maker, or if the parent invests in the plant.
look_again_if: Look again if a listing names cryocoolers, if the parent changes hands, or if the yen moves more than 15% against the dollar.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means negotiating from a queue, and in Future 4 the whole gap is left uncovered.

name: Confirm the export-control classifications of wire, cold heads and logic parts, and the China plant's export license approval rate
protects: It protects the wire, the cold heads, the logic parts and the China plant. Future 3 and Future 4 rest on export classifications nobody has checked, and magnet-grade wire has never been checked against the dual-use export lists.
why_now: It costs nothing, and it decides whether the China plant stock (A5) and the second logic source (A6) are sound bets or wasted money. The Geopolitical and Foreign trade and payments members proposed it independently.
too_late_after: It is too late after the truce notice date.
act_if: Act now, whatever the indicators show.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again at every revision of the export-control lists.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means A5 and A6 are bought against a guess, and the only wire source sits under a rule nobody has read.

name: Run an annual credit and ownership watch on the wire mill and the cold-head parent
protects: It protects the wire and the cold head. Question 1 counts an owner leaving the business as a stop, and an exit shows up in filings before it reaches the press.
why_now: It costs very little. The cold-head parent's share of revenue from MR is itself a Placeholder.
too_late_after: It is too late once a sale is announced.
act_if: Act if either parent's revenue from the relevant business falls under 5% of the group's revenue.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again if ownership changes.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means an exit is seen in the press instead of in the filings a year earlier.

name: Test one hazard against several sites at once: one hurricane against the plant, the port and the helium shipping routes together, and one Nankai Trough earthquake against the cold-head and compressor makers together
protects: It protects the United States plant, the export port, the gas carriers, the oversize road route, the cold-head maker and the compressor maker. The starting list of actions tested sites one at a time, and weather does not strike one site at a time.
why_now: The continuity plan tests sites one at a time. One Atlantic storm can close three sites in a month.
too_late_after: It is too late after the 2027 hurricane season.
act_if: Act if the continuity plan still tests sites one at a time.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again after each named storm.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves a season exposed to a stop that single-site plans do not see.

name: Qualify a source of logic parts that does not originate in the United States for the Asian build
protects: It protects the supply of logic parts and the China plant. It shortens the Future 3 stop rather than preventing it, because 18 months from early 2027 ends at or after the failure, and a part made abroad can still be caught by the United States foreign direct product rule. Five panel members add Future 4, where it shortens the license queue. The Contrarian member notes that it gives up some ownership of the design.
why_now: Only a start in the first quarter of 2027 finishes before 2029.
too_late_after: It is too late after mid-2027.
act_if: Act if an entity listing names the China plant's logic supplier, or if export license approvals stay below half for two quarters.
pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed with no listing, or if the China plant stock (A5) covers the license queue.
look_again_if: Look again if the foreign direct product rule reaches this product class, or if a second chip foundry clears equivalent parts.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year gives a 2029 answer to a 2027 failure, and the Future 3 stop runs the whole license queue.

name: Size ramp-up and test capacity at the United States plant to cover part of the Asian build
owner: Site operations with the Install PMO
protects: It protects the China plant's customers. It is the only action that keeps an Asian delivery date when the China plant stops. It does nothing in Future 1, where the United States plant itself fails, and it raises that plant's helium use, so the 2027 capital plan must size it together with the helium stock (A3).
why_now: Capacity takes 24 months to change (AI-suggested, Site operations to confirm), and the 2027 capital plan is the only chance to fund it. The Financial member judged that it ties up more working capital than any other action on the list.
too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
act_if: Act if a listing names the China plant or its logic supplier, or if the plant's stock falls below the length of the license queue.
pause_if: Pause if the truce is renewed through 2028, or if a second Asian site is approved.
look_again_if: Look again if the helium on hand cannot carry the extra use, if there are not enough technicians to staff a second shift, or if Asian tenders add local-content rules.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year loses an Asian tender cycle, and in Future 3 the route that would supply Asia is not ready for two more years.

name: Design and test a hold that keeps a sealed magnet cold for 30 days without a working cold head
protects: It protects the cold head and the installed sealed magnets. The Contrarian member notes that the physics may not allow it, so the first step is a cheap study.
why_now: It matters once sealed magnets pass half of output, which the panel expects in 2029.
start_by: With a study in 2027 and the design by 2028
too_late_after: It is too late once sealed magnets pass half of output.
act_if: Act if sealed magnets pass a quarter of new builds, or if the study shows that a hold of more than 30 days is possible.
pause_if: Pause if A1 qualifies a second maker, or if the study shows a hold of under 10 days.
look_again_if: Look again when Engineering states the test draw, or if a conduction-cooled design appears in clearances.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting costs little until 2028. After that, each year leaves the sealed magnets in the field with no hold.

name: Build a skilled-trades hiring pipeline at the United States plant before the sealed-magnet conversion decision (A11)
protects: It protects the technicians and the United States plant. Competence takes 18 months to build, and nobody has measured when the current technicians will retire. A skill that has retired cannot be bought back the way a part can.
why_now: The conventional and sealed lines need different skilled trades, and hiring for 2029 starts in 2027.
too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
act_if: Act if more than a quarter of magnet winders and cryogenic technicians will retire within five years.
pause_if: Pause if automation takes winding off the factory floor.
look_again_if: Look again if a competing local employer closes.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a group of new hires who are not competent until 2030.

name: Map labor contract expiry dates at the plants, the hub and the ports against storm and winter seasons
protects: It protects the plants, the hub and the export port. The longshore master contract expires on 30 Sep 2030, inside the hurricane season, and a port contract expiring in a storm month means two stops at once.
why_now: It takes a week of work and needs nothing to be bought.
too_late_after: It is too late at the next port contract expiry.
act_if: Act if any contract expires in 2027 or 2028.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again every year.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year lets a known date arrive without a plan.

name: Rewrite delivery clauses, agree a late-delivery remedy script and publish delivery performance before health systems do
owner: Install PMO (project management office) with the S&OP (sales and operations planning) council
protects: It protects market share. It changes what a late install costs, not whether it happens, and all four futures push installs past the 30-day limit somewhere. No public tender framework that the panel retrieved scores delivery reliability explicitly, so whether tenders score late delivery at all is unverified.
why_now: Hospital purchasing frameworks renew on multi-year cycles.
too_late_after: It is too late once a health system publishes delivery scores first.
act_if: Act if a large customer adds delivery scoring.
pause_if: Pause if tenders never score reliability.
look_again_if: Look again if competitors publish their delivery performance first.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves a cycle of delivery scores the OEM does not manage, and the market share lost at the first install more than 30 days late.

name: Set an allocation rule for scarce magnets
protects: It protects market share where the OEM is one of two or three suppliers. In every future it changes the cost of a stop, not whether the stop happens.
why_now: Without a rule, the first stop will allocate scarce magnets by order date.
too_late_after: It is too late after the first stop.
act_if: Act if any plant stops.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again if tender scoring changes.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means the first stop allocates magnets by order date.

name: Pre-permit an oversize road route to a second export port and hold helium there before each hurricane season
protects: It protects the export port and the gas carriers. It reduces delays in all four futures, and it prevents a stop only in Future 1 and Future 3, where the helium held at the port matters.
why_now: Hurricane season comes every year, and the single port closes for days in every future.
too_late_after: It is too late after a port closure of more than 10 days.
act_if: Act if the port closes for 10 days, or if its records show a stop of more than 10 days.
pause_if: Pause if a second berth is contracted, or if the helium on hand outlasts the longest closure.
look_again_if: Look again after any bridge weight restriction on the route, or if the second port lies on the same storm track.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks a season of held exports.

name: Contract a second carrier for liquid helium, with an inland transfer point
protects: It protects the gas carriers and the helium on hand. A systems outage at a carrier uses up the helium on hand and stops the plant for 50 to 60 days (panel estimate).
why_now: One carrier handles most deliveries (basis not stated).
too_late_after: It is too late after a carrier outage.
act_if: Act if one carrier handles more than two thirds of deliveries.
pause_if: Pause if the plant holds 90 days of helium on hand.
look_again_if: Look again every year.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves another year exposed to a carrier failure.

name: Fix helium allocation priority in writing, indexed to a published price, on a shipping route that avoids the Gulf strait and sanctioned payment systems
protects: It protects the helium supply and the helium on hand. The price at which the OEM loses its allocation is a Placeholder, and without a written priority the helium stock in A3 cannot be built at allocated volumes.
why_now: A chip plant can take priority over the OEM at any time.
too_late_after: It is too late once a buyers' market returns or a chip plant takes priority.
act_if: Act if a chip plant is reported taking priority, or if Qatar's share of United States helium imports falls further.
pause_if: Pause if the Gulf strait reopens and a buyers' market returns.
look_again_if: Look again at each allocation letter.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year could make the helium stock in A3 impossible to build.

name: Hedge the yen exposure on cold heads and compressors for the contract term
protects: It protects the bill for cold heads and compressors. It smooths costs in every future.
why_now: It starts when the supply agreement (A2) is signed.
too_late_after: It is too late once the parent company reprices.
act_if: Act if the Bank of Japan changes its interest rate path.
pause_if: Pause if the supply agreement (A2) is priced in dollars.
look_again_if: Look again every year.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year costs little.

name: Map the cold head's own suppliers before signing a second maker
protects: It protects the cold head. A second maker that relies on the same suppliers for regenerators and displacers (parts inside the cold head) gives only the appearance of a second source.
why_now: It is a study of a few months, and the second maker (A1) should not be signed until it is done.
too_late_after: It is too late once A1 is signed.
act_if: Act when A1 starts.
pause_if: Pause if the maker shows that its inputs come from two sources.
look_again_if: Look again at each qualification.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting means A1 may buy a second source that shares the first one's suppliers.

name: Buy contingent business interruption insurance naming the wire mill, the cold-head maker and the helium supply
protects: It pays toward the bill for a failure but does not prevent one, and only if insurers will write the policy. Cyber insurance already excludes acts by states.
why_now: Insurers are withdrawing capacity for this kind of policy.
too_late_after: It is too late after a loss.
act_if: Act if a broker quotes a policy that names the suppliers.
pause_if: Pause if exclusions would void the policy.
look_again_if: Look again if the premium costs more than the China plant stock in A5.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year leaves one more year uninsured.

name: Require counterfeit-avoidance and cyber attestation from sole suppliers and carriers
protects: It protects the wire, the cold head, the electronics, the carriers and the port. Attestation must not replace the manual fallback exercise in A9.
why_now: Future 4 adds the cost of grey-market cold heads, and attackers rarely get in through the OEM's own network.
too_late_after: It is too late once a counterfeit part reaches a magnet.
act_if: Act if a counterfeit alert names any kind of component on the supplier map.
pause_if: Do not pause this action.
look_again_if: Look again at each sourcing cycle.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year means a year of unverified parts.

name: Decide how fast the OEM converts to sealed magnets, including whether the 3 tesla line converts
protects: This decision sets which pair of futures the line operates in. Converting trades a dependency on the Gulf (helium on hand) for one on Japan (the cold head). Waiting a year chooses Future 1 and Future 3 by default. Conversion makes A1 and A9 more valuable if it means one part keeps every magnet cold.
why_now: The 2027 capital plan is the next chance to decide. The conventional and sealed lines need different skilled trades, and hiring for 2029 starts in 2027.
too_late_after: It is too late after 2028.
act_if: Act if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder and a 3 tesla sealed clearance is filed.
pause_if: Pause if hospitals decline the first sealed option, if the test draw is the size of a full delivery, or if no second cold-head source exists.
look_again_if: Look again if helium returns to a buyers' market, if a competitor gets a 3 tesla sealed magnet cleared, or if tenders score independence from helium.
cost_of_waiting: Waiting a year risks hiring the wrong trades or none, and one more year on helium's terms.
